t:
Section 101(b) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1101(b)) is amended—

    (1) 
in paragraph (1)—

        (A) 
in subparagraph (A), by striking “legitimate child and inserting “child born in wedlock”; and
 
        (B) 
in subparagraph (D), by striking “an illegitimate child” and inserting “a child born out of wedlock”; and
  
    (2) 
in paragraph (2), by striking “an illegitimate child” and inserting “a child born out of wedlock”.

fable.w: This section only makes terminology amendments to the Immigration and Nationality Act, replacing "legitimate" and "illegitimate child" with "child born in wedlock" and "child born out of wedlock". There is no tempting reading here: it provides for no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government.

opus.w: This section only replaces outdated terms in the definitions of 'child' in 8 U.S.C. 1101(b) with neutral language. It creates no comment period, rulemaking authority, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation or right to sue. Amending an immigration statute does not by that alone bring outside parties into a federal decision.
opus.b: I found no participation here. One possible wrong reading is to treat any amendment to the Immigration and Nationality Act as touching on agency decisions about immigration status. But this section only changes wording ("illegitimate child" becomes "child born out of wedlock"). It sets up no process that involves anyone outside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section solely amends the statutory definitions of 'child' and 'illegitimate child' within the Immigration and Nationality Act. It does not establish any mechanism for consultation, coordination, or participation by non-federal entities (such as the public, states, or experts) in federal decision-making. The changes are purely textual and definitional, affecting eligibility criteria rather than procedural participation.
qwen_chat.s: Section 101(b) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1101(b)) is amended— (1) in paragraph (1)— (A) in subparagraph (A), by striking “legitimate child and inserting “child born in wedlock”; and (B) in subparagraph (D), by striking “an illegitimate child” and inserting “a child born out of wedlock”; and (2) in paragraph (2), by striking “an illegitimate child” and inserting “a child born out of wedlock”.
qwen_chat.b:
Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing definitions affects who can participate in immigration processes, but the text itself is purely definitional and does not establish any process for outside parties to consult with or influence the government.
Resolution: The section only amends statutory definitions of "child" and "illegitimate child." It does not create any advisory bodies, comment periods, hearings, or consultation requirements with non-federal entities.
